question: Can optimizing a single global Chernoff exponent and retaining path direction make the existing nonbacktracking path-sum route bound the physical H12 contrast at p=.30 and finite h?
role: Smallest deterministic falsification of a candidate H12 estimate outside the certified wedges; no physical data acquisition.
hypotheses: A direction-weighted nonbacktracking transfer has spectral radius below one for some 0<s<1 and finite h, giving a summable physical-record path bound.
Its spectral radius is at least one for all 0<s<1 and finite h at p=.30, so this entire fixed-global-exponent path-sum route is inconclusive there.
frozen_model: Canonical square U(1) current channel, a=1-p, b=pq, c=p(1-q), q=(1+tanh h)/2; physical measured Q and true H12 Bayes contrast remain the estimand.
registered_method: For a unit path shift use Chernoff factors u_s=a^(1-s)b^s+c^(1-s)a^s and v_s=a^(1-s)c^s+b^(1-s)a^s. Form the four-direction nonbacktracking transfer T_ij=w_j unless j reverses i, with w=(u_s,u_s,v_s,v_s). Prove or refute an analytic lower bound on rho(T), and check p=.30 at q=.5,.75,.97,1 and s=.25,.5,.75. The q=1 endpoint is a mathematical limiting control, not a finite-h claim.
acceptance: Exact inequality with independently checked arithmetic and explicit scope. If rho>=1, close only the fixed-global-Chernoff nonbacktracking summability shortcut, not H12 correctability, optimized path-dependent exponents, or phase boundaries.
stop_rule: Stop after the analytic inequality and registered 12-cell arithmetic. Keep the p=.30 H12 target open regardless of method outcome.
decision: The fixed-global-exponent nonbacktracking certificate cannot be summable at p=.30 for any finite h; rho is minimized by s=1/2 and is at least 1.374772708487 even at q=1. This is a method obstruction, not an H12 phase result.
